summary: Vinod Mishra is an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.Sc. at Kurukshetra University (1989–1991) and a Ph.D. at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (1994–1998), becoming a professor at Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology in 2010.
Vipul Jadav is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. in Sanskrit at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University (2017–2021). He became an assistant professor there in 2020.
Virchand Gandhi (1864–1901) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai (~1880–1884) and taught Herbert Warren.
Virendra Kumar Varma is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.
Virendra Kumar Verma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra. He later taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935–2015) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961), later serving as director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1984–2000).

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) studied in Mumbai, Cambridge, Edinburgh, and Berlin (Ph.D. under Heinrich Lüders). He served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI in 1925.

Vishva Bandhu (1897–1973), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Alfred Cooper Woolner (~1918–1920). He was founder-principal at Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921) and served as director at DAV College (1934) and the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1950–1973).

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Elphinstone College (~1847–1852). He was an examiner at the University of Mumbai (~1862) and vice-president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1874–1889).

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1944–1946), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1946–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram Universities. He directed Scindia Oriental Institute (~1972–1985), was vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1986–1989, 1992–1995) and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1996–1998), and chaired ICPR (1997).

Vitalij Petrovič Furnika (1940–1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Semën Gesselevič Rudin (1965), at Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1970), and at the University of Madras (1969–1970).

Vittore Pisani (1899–1990) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Sapienza University of Rome (1921). He held professorships at the Universities of Cagliari (1935–1938), Milan (1938–1969), and Bocconi (1946–1966).
Vittorio Bettei was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts as a teacher of Latin and Greek at Liceo Ginnasio Benedetto Cairoli and Liceo Canova.

Vittorio Rocca (1862–1905) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa (~1880–1885). He served as a docent at Sapienza University of Rome (~1895–1905) and held a libera docenza in Sanskrit at Pisa (1905).

Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He lectured at Vienna (2022–2025) before joining the Austrian Academy of Sciences as a researcher (2025–2026).

Vlad Bănățeanu (1900–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Chernivtsi, Bucharest, EPHE, and INALCO under Meillet, Benveniste, and others. He later held posts at Chernivtsi University (1932) and the University of Bucharest (~1957–1963).

Vladimir Aleksandrovich Chernyshev (1927–1999) was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Moscow State University (~1948–1953), he taught at MGIMO (1952–1956) and joined the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1956.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).
